factor: Headward fluid shift and lower blood pressure
mechanism: Loss of gravity moves blood and fluid toward the chest and head; heart fills more; blood vessels widen (vascular resistance down 39%)
onset: Present when measured at flight day 85-192
measurable_signs: Stroke volume +35%, cardiac output +41%, 24 h BP 8-10 mmHg lower, heart rate unchanged
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 24 h systolic about 121 mmHg, diastolic about 76 mmHg (mean of 8 men)
warning_signs: Authors link the high cardiac output to possible vision problems (see SANS row)
quote: Cardiac stroke volume and output increased by 35 ± 10% and 41 ± 9% ( P < 0.001)

mechanism: Routine ISS exercise keeps resting heart rate, BP and baroreflex stable in flight
onset: Measured early and late in 2-6 month missions
measurable_signs: Resting HR and BP unchanged; stroke volume and pulse pressure lower
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: HR and BP similar to own preflight values
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: The current program routine of countermeasures on the International Space Station provided sufficient stimulus to maintain cardiovascular stability under resting conditions

mechanism: Cardiovascular deconditioning grows with flight length
onset: Landing day; recovery slower after ISS than Shuttle
measurable_signs: Cannot complete a 10 min 80 degree head-up tilt test (fainting or near-fainting)
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Only 2 of 6 ISS astronauts completed tilt test on landing day; 13 of 15 by day 3
warning_signs: Light-headedness on standing after return (implied by tilt test failure)
countermeasure: Plan reduced activities and more medical support after long missions
quote: The proportion of astronauts who completed the OTT on R+0 (2 of 6) was less in ISS than in Shuttle astronauts (52 of 65).

mechanism: Vestibular (inner ear) and fluid-shift changes; several combined hypotheses including sensory conflict
onset: First days of flight (exact window not stated in this abstract)
measurable_signs: Nausea, vomiting, headache, loss of appetite, pallor
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Incidence on Space Shuttle about 67%
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: "Space motion sickness" is a autonomic syndrome that exhibits nausea, vomiting, headache, anorexia, pallor etc., whose incidence in Space Shuttle mission reaches 67.1%.

mechanism: See previous row
onset: First Shuttle flight; less common on second flight (46%)
measurable_signs: Graded mild, moderate or severe by flight surgeon
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 67% of first-flight crew: 30% mild, 24% moderate, 13% severe
warning_signs: Severe grade in 13% of first-flight crew
quote: The incidence of SMS during a first Shuttle flight for 85 crewmembers was 67% (57 cases).

mechanism: Unloading; in-flight exercise loads lower than on Earth (in-shoe forces 46-50% lower)
measurable_signs: Calf volume -10 to -16%, thigh -4 to -7%, knee strength -10.4 to -24.1%
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Upper arm volume unchanged (+0.4 to -0.8%)
warning_signs: not stated in this source
countermeasure: Exercise on ISS, but authors say it was not enough and loads should increase
quote: Muscle volume change was greater in the calf (-10 to 16%) than the thigh (-4% to -7%)

mechanism: Unloading of the skeleton
measurable_signs: DXA bone density loss at spine and hip (not measurable on board)
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Spine about 0.9%/month, hip about 1.4-1.5%/month (14 ISS crew, 4-6 months)
warning_signs: not stated in this source
countermeasure: Exercise (later work: ARED plus bisphosphonate reduced loss, see LeBlanc 2013, PMID 23334732)
quote: aBMD was lost at rates of 0.9%/month at the spine (p < 0.001) and 1.4-1.5%/month at the hip (p < 0.001).

mechanism: Linked to headward fluid shift; exact cause unknown
measurable_signs: Optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal and retinal folds, hyperopic (far-sighted) shift, cotton wool spots
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: About 15% had clinically significant optic disc edema; choroidal folds in over 20%
warning_signs: Change in near vision; headaches in SANS are mild or occasional
countermeasure: Under study; none proven in this source
quote: To date approximately 15% of astronauts had clinically significant (Frisén grade 1–3) ODE after LDSF

mechanism: Possibly linked to low-grade inflammation (IL-1ra rise) and impaired heat loss
onset: Rises over about 2.5 months, then plateaus
measurable_signs: Resting core temperature up about 1 °C; faster rise during exercise
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: About +1 °C above own preflight resting core temperature
warning_signs: Exercise core temperature above 40 °C in some crew
quote: This increase of about 1 °C developed gradually over 2.5 months and was associated with augmented concentrations of interleukin-1 receptor antagonist

factor: Immune dysregulation and latent herpes virus reactivation
mechanism: Stress hormones up and cell-mediated immunity down, so latent viruses reactivate
onset: Seen on 10-16 day Shuttle and 180+ day ISS flights; did not fade with longer missions
measurable_signs: Virus shedding in saliva/urine (lab test, not on board); sometimes skin lesions or dermatitis
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 61% of ISS astronauts (14/23) shed one or more herpes viruses
warning_signs: Skin lesions or rash (live virus recovered in some cases)
countermeasure: None proven; authors call for countermeasures
quote: Currently, 47/89 (53%) astronauts from shuttle-flights and 14/23 (61%) astronauts from ISS missions shed one or more herpes viruses

mechanism: Fluid shift, muscle and bone loss, immune, gut and liver enzyme changes may change drug handling; drug stability may also drop
measurable_signs: Not measurable by crew
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Few in-flight PK data exist
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: Few inflight pharmacokinetic data have been published, and pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic studies during spaceflight are also lacking.

mechanism: Adaptation to microgravity (spine unloading)
measurable_signs: Self-reported back pain
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 52% of astronauts; of those 86% mild, 11% moderate, 3% severe
warning_signs: Moderate or severe pain not responding to treatment risks mission impact
countermeasure: Fetal (knees-to-chest) position 91% effective; analgesics and exercise 85%
quote: The most effective treatments were fetal positioning (91%) and the use of analgesic medications and exercise

mechanism: Causes not analysed in this source; sleep medication use was common
onset: Whole mission; no trend over ISS missions
measurable_signs: Actigraphy or sleep log hours
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 6.09 ± 0.67 h/night on ISS (mean ± SD)
warning_signs: Under 6 h on 43.8% of ISS nights
countermeasure: Sleep medication used by 75% of ISS crew at some point
quote: 75% of ISS crewmembers (12/16) reported using sleep-promoting medications

mechanism: Isolation, confinement, workload, distance from family, monotony
onset: Any time; analog data suggest a later-mission dip
measurable_signs: Mood or anxiety disturbance, sleep change, crew conflict
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Low incidence; no behavioral emergency reported in spaceflight to 2016
warning_signs: Decrement in mood, cognition, morale or interpersonal interaction that affects readiness
countermeasure: Private psychological conferences, family contact, support
quote: While mood and anxiety disturbances have occurred, no behavioral emergencies have been reported to date in space flight.

mechanism: Stress, sleep loss, CO2, medications, head injury can reduce attention and memory
measurable_signs: WinSCAT score vs own baseline
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Own preflight baseline; taken monthly in orbit
warning_signs: Off-nominal WinSCAT score
countermeasure: Crew surgeon review; adjust work-rest schedule
quote: Baseline testing begins 6 months before launch, and the astronaut is requested to take it once a month while in orbit.

mechanism: Cabin CO2 runs far above Earth air; poor air mixing in microgravity
onset: Hours to days of raised CO2
measurable_signs: Headache reports linked to CO2 level
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: ISS CO2 1-9 mmHg (at time of study)
warning_signs: Headache; odds double per +1 mmHg CO2
countermeasure: Keep 7-day average CO2 below 2.5 mmHg for headache risk under 1%
quote: For each 1-mm Hg increase in CO(2), the odds of a crew member reporting a headache doubled.

mechanism: Hypercapnia
measurable_signs: Headache, fatigue, malaise, flushing
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004]: 1-hour average ppCO2 no more than 3 mmHg
warning_signs: Headaches reported at 2.8-4.5 mmHg, worse with higher CO2
quote: Headaches at levels between 2.8-4.5 mmHg; worsening

mechanism: Galactic cosmic rays and solar particles raise long-term cancer and other risks
measurable_signs: Dosimeter dose (crew cannot feel it)
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Career effective dose under 600 mSv
warning_signs: None felt at career-level doses
quote: total career effective radiation dose due to space flight radiation exposure shall be less than 600 mSv

mechanism: Solar proton storms
onset: Hours to days during an event
measurable_signs: Sudden dose rate rise on area monitors and personal dosimeters
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Design SPE dose under 250 mSv effective
warning_signs: Radiation alarm or ground SPE alert
countermeasure: Shelter in the most shielded area
quote: environment proton energy spectrum (sum of the October 1989 events) to less than a NASA effective dose of 250 mSv

factor: Acute radiation sickness risk in a large SPE
mechanism: High dose over hours if not sheltered
measurable_signs: Prodromal symptoms (e.g. nausea) in a historically large event
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Most SPEs harmless
warning_signs: Prodromal symptoms; unprotected for over 2 hours in a large event
quote: Radiation sickness possible if unprotected >2 hours

mechanism: Blood-forming organ dose
measurable_signs: Nausea; low white cell count
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: BFO limit 250 mGy-Eq (draft Artemis rules, up to 30 days)
warning_signs: Nausea in 50% at about 1000 mGy-Eq; white cell drop at about 500 mGy-Eq
quote: White blood cell count depression 500 mGy-eq • Nausea (50% population) 1000 mGy-eq

mechanism: GCR plus trapped protons in the South Atlantic Anomaly
measurable_signs: Dosimeter readings
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: 0.2-0.5 mSv/day effective; about 40-90 mSv per 6 months
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: effective doses accumulate at a rate of approximately 0.2 to 0.5 mSv/day

factor: Distance from Earth: communication delay and self-sufficiency
mechanism: Distance makes help, supplies and medical care slow or impossible
onset: Mars missions about 3 years round trip
measurable_signs: Comms delay
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Up to 20 minutes one-way delay to Mars
warning_signs: Medical emergency during comms delay or loss
quote: Facing a communication delay of up to 20 minutes one way, the possibility of equipment failures or medical emergencies

mechanism: Resistive and aerobic exercise to slow muscle, bone and fitness loss
measurable_signs: Minutes logged per device
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: About 2 hours exercise per day on ARED, T2 treadmill, CEVIS cycle
warning_signs: not stated in this source
countermeasure: ARED (resistive), T2 treadmill, CEVIS cycle ergometer
quote: with crew members now averaging two hours of exercise per day

mechanism: Harness and bungee loading gives lower forces than 1 g exercise
measurable_signs: In-shoe force
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Running and cycling forces about 46% and 50% lower than 1 g
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: The peak in-shoe forces during running and cycling on ISS were approximately 46% and 50% lower compared to 1-g values.

mechanism: Functional adaptation (authors)
measurable_signs: Respiratory frequency
normal_inflight_range_with_unit: Lower than preflight (value NOT FOUND in abstract)
warning_signs: not stated in this source
quote: The decreases in BP and RF combined with stable HR and HRV during flight suggest functional adaptation rather than pathological changes.
